speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry can provide an update on the adequacy of the supply of school bus services; (b) whether an update on the same can be provided specifically for Special Education schools; and (c) what is the average increase in school bus fares seen in 2022.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) has been monitoring the provision of school bus services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Despite these challenges, most providers have continued providing school bus services, but have to raise their fares to reflect both rising costs and the need for the industry to attract and retain sufficient school bus drivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: These are issues which MOE is engaging with the relevant stakeholders to address.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: This will reduce the amount paid by the families of these needy students and help mitigate the increase in school bus fares.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Beyond that, in situations where the family needs more help, the schools are able to provide more financial assistance to cover the school bus fares.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Beyond that, the SPED schools are able to provide further discretionary support to needy students who may need additional help with their school bus fares.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Both the Ministry of Social and Family Development and MOE will continue to closely monitor the school bus fare situation, and if need be, step up the financial support for needy students who have to travel by school bus.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My understanding of the school bus operator population is that – and I will stand corrected if this is not borne out by the facts – but my understanding is that we have an ageing population and many of these operators are set up as sole proprietorships.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: They may employ a very small number of people or may drive the buses themselves.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Over time, we can expect that there will be exits from the industry.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Is the Ministry looking at how to address that?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Because as the population ages, there could be certain solutions that we need to look at.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: For example, facilitating owners of micro businesses to sell their business to a more organised operator – I just mentioned that as one possibility.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My second supplementary question is on the school bus services for SPED schools.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I wanted to ask what sort of training is made available to the bus operators for SPED schools, given the complexity involved, which is different from just operating a bus for mainstream schools.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Sometimes, there could be certain types of skills that they need to have in order to do their job effectively.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I have encountered one issue with one of my constituents in the Serangoon ward of the Aljunied Group Representative Constituency.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: So, I am wondering what sort of training is given to these bus operators.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Indeed, the school bus industry is quite a fragmented one, with many sole proprietors.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We at MOE ourselves are also beginning to learn about this industry and we are in discussion with other agencies.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We are starting to engage the school bus operators to see what kind of help we can provide to facilitate this industry to stay viable in the long term and to support the needs of our students for school bus services.
